reasoning: Every real square is nonnegative, so S>=0. Set r=sqrt(S); r^2=S follows from nonnegative mass, while S>0 gives r>0 and S!=0.
Finite distributivity gives sum_b(f(b)/r)^2=(sum_b f(b)^2)/r^2=S/S=1. Signs of the entries play no role.

At S=0 every entry is zero; no proportional unit vector exists. Empty index sets cannot satisfy S>0. A zero-qubit index set has one element, and a negative nonzero scalar normalizes to -1. Lean totalized division does not make a zero table unit length.
limitations: Source text inspection and NL reasoning only; no new compilation.
Any shared normalization-domain fragments with A2 remain disclosed and are not independent held-out evidence.

reasoning: J†J=I and P=JJ† is an orthogonal projector. With ell=(I-P)UJpsi, UJpsi=JBpsi+ell, J†ell=0 and ||Bpsi||^2+||ell||^2=1. Born success is p=||Bpsi||^2. J†, and consequently the clean compression B, are contractions.

My independent route used x=Apsi, y=alpha Bpsi. The delivered equivalent route uses x=Apsi/alpha, y=Bpsi, delta=epsilon/alpha. Operator action bounds the raw difference and reverse triangle proves ||Bpsi||>=(s-epsilon)/alpha>0, so all normalized vectors and p>0 are justified.

Positive alpha removes any phase factor from normalization. The supplied stability lemma and unit-vector triangle give min(2,2epsilon/s). Squaring nonnegative norm bounds and using B contraction gives the requested success interval.

With r=s/alpha and q=||Bpsi||, |q-r|<=epsilon/alpha and q+r<=2s/alpha+epsilon/alpha give the probability-error bound epsilon(2s+epsilon)/alpha^2. U=I, alpha=1, A=(1+epsilon)I shows the nominal s^2/alpha^2 can exceed one.

Independent fresh trials have geometric first-success time, with expected count 1/p for each preparation, U call and test, bounded by alpha^2/(s-epsilon)^2. Preparation and testing are charged; no inverse or amplification access is assumed.

The exact case may still have p<1. At s=0 the target is undefined; approximate accepted norm is at most epsilon/alpha. At the weakened threshold s=epsilon>0, U=X tensor I, alpha=1, A=epsilon I gives B=0 and p=0. For m=0, P=I and p=1. For n=0, H is one-dimensional, not zero-dimensional. Another procedure may prepare a target such as psi for A=cI without postselection.

reasoning: For c=(a+b)/4 and h=(a-b)/4, cosine and sine sum-difference formulas give R(a)-R(b)=2 sin(h)[[-sin(c),-cos(c)],[cos(c),-sin(c)]]=2 sin((a-b)/4)R((a+b)/2+pi).

The last matrix is unitary and has induced norm one, so the exact distance is 2|sin((a-b)/4)|. The scalar sign belongs in the matrix identity; absolute value enters only on taking its norm. |sin t|<=|t| gives the |a-b|/2 bound.

An identity spectator tensor gives the same scalar times a joint unitary on nonzero dimension 2 times 2^r, which has induced norm one even on entangled inputs. Common wire reindexing is unitary conjugation and preserves the norm.
Zero spectators recovers the one-qubit calculation. Zero total qubits have no target wire. Angle differences 4pi k give identical matrices, whereas odd multiples of 2pi give exact distance two.
